symptom: `move enumeration Shop.Status to Other;` printed "Updated enumeration references" and "Moved enumeration", but every reference outside the domain models kept naming the old module: mx check reported CE1613 at a parameter of the enumeration type, a create-variable activity (type and value), an end event returning an enumeration value, and the microflow's return type. Entity attributes of the type were updated (ako/mxcli#1674, split out of ako/mxcli#1671)
cause: execMove's dispatch did `return moveEnumeration(…)` for an enumeration, returning before the shared `if isCrossModuleMove { updateQualifiedNameRefs(…) }` sweep that every other document's cross-module move falls through to. moveEnumeration itself only called UpdateEnumerationRefsInAllDomainModels
insight: When one kind of a shared operation misbehaves, look for an early `return` in the dispatch before the code every case relies on: here two cases returned early, and only one of them (moveEntity) ran its own sweep. The domain-model update the enumeration case did print made the move look complete, so the entity attribute is the right control in a test and not evidence of success. The sweep is whole-value only on its own; an enumeration value inside a longer expression also needs the expression-aware rewrite of ako/mxcli#1671 (measured: this fix alone leaves CE0117 on `$In = X.Open or …`, both together 0 errors)
